issues.failure_explanation: For a subsonic extended source moving toward the observer, far-field arrival-time intervals for consecutive impulses can overlap even when $t_j-t_{j-1}>\mathrm{diam}(D_{j-1})/c$; the stated condition lacks the displacement and the next-support terms needed to exclude overlap. Thus the claimed separability is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: The second assumption ensures that wave signals generated at different instants remain separable due to non-overlapping supports. This can be rigourously derived from the explicit expression of $U(x, t)$ in terms of the convolution of $\tilde{S}$ and the fundamental solution $G$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen Assumption \ref{sump} with an arrival-time non-overlap condition involving both supports and the displacement of $a$, and prove the separation; or remove the separability claim.
issues.overall_effect: The justification for extracting separate data $u_j^\infty$ from a single recorded far field, and the multi-impulse corollary relying on it, are unreliable.
issues.title: Separability under the time-gap assumption is not guaranteed
issues.why_classification: A repair requires a new nontrivial separation argument or a changed parameter regime, but it does not alter the single-impulse theory if the claim is removed.

issues.failure_explanation: The wave equation uses speed $c$, but the displayed solution integrates over $|x-y|=t-t_0$ with denominator $4\pi(t-t_0)$; for $c\neq1$ the correct surface is $|x-y|=c(t-t_0)$ with denominator $4\pi c(t-t_0)$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor $c$ in the integration surface and denominator, or explicitly set $c=1$ in this subsection.
issues.overall_effect: The time-domain representation of the single-impulse field is incorrect unless $c=1$ is silently assumed.
issues.title: Retarded wave expression omits wave speed c
issues.why_classification: A local parameter omission does not affect the frequency-domain proofs if corrected.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only obtains norm convergence $\mathcal{F}_\epsilon\to F$, but norm convergence of positive operators does not imply equality of the ranges of their square roots. The displayed limit of ranges is asserted without a nontrivial argument, and the measure statement $\mathrm{meas}(D\setminus \overline{Y}_\epsilon)\to0$ is reversed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either impose the original strict positivity condition $|S|\ge c>0$ and apply the cited theorem directly, or add a valid range-convergence lemma for $\mathcal{F}_{\epsilon,\#}^{1/2}\to F_{\#}^{1/2}$.
issues.overall_effect: The range identity used for Picard's theorem and all indicator-function results is unsupported under the relaxed a.e.-positivity assumption.
issues.title: Range identity proof does not justify passing to the limit
issues.why_classification: The result can be salvaged by a contained additional argument or by reverting to the stronger positivity hypothesis, but the claimed relaxation is not established as written.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof of Lemma \ref{supplu} is similar to the proof of \cite[Lemma 3.1]{GGH2022}.

issues.failure_explanation: $L$ is defined as an operator into $L^2(0,K)$. The inverse Fourier transform of an $L^2(0,K)$ function, under the stated transform convention, is taken after zero extension to $\R$ and is not compactly supported in the $q$-variable. The support inclusion holds only for the full Fourier transform/entire extension, not for the finite-band range element as used in the paper.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify and prove the correct analytic-extension/Paley-Wiener interpretation of $\mathcal{F}^{-1}(Lu)$ for elements of $\mathrm{Range}(L)$, or replace the lemma with a valid finite-band argument.
issues.overall_effect: The support-based contradiction argument in the proof of the pointwise test-function theorem is invalid.
issues.title: Support lemma for inverse Fourier transform of finite-band $Lu$ is false as written
issues.why_classification: The lemma can be repaired by clarifying the meaning of the inverse transform, but the repair requires a nontrivial analytic argument and the lemma as written is false.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Choose the set $\{y_m\}_{m=1}^{\infty}$ such that $y=y_1$.Then we have $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L_N)$ for all $N\geq 1$. By Lemma \ref{lem4.1} (ii), it holds that $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing $q(y)=c^{-1}\hat{x}\cdot y-t_0$, the range of $L$ consists of Fourier transforms of $L^2$ functions of $q$ over the projection of $D$. The test function $e^{-i\tau b}$ would correspond to the Dirac measure at $q=b$, which is not an $L^2$ function. Hence $\phi_{z,\eta}$ is not in $\mathrm{Range}(L)$ even when $b$ lies in the projection of $D$; the proof only establishes membership in a closure.

failure_location.quote: For any $\eta \in \R$, there holds $z \in {K}_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}$ if and only if $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the false range-membership criterion with a valid finite-band characterization or a different indicator, or prove that the relevant pointwise exponentials actually lie in the stated range.
issues.overall_effect: The central pointwise criterion for strips, and all indicator-based reconstruction and uniqueness results built on it, are invalid as stated.
issues.title: Pointwise test function is not characterized by membership in Range($L$)
issues.why_classification: The main advertised pointwise test-function theorem fails and no comparable source-supported version of the stated range-membership criterion survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \tcr{There exists} $ N_0 \in \mathbb{Z}_+ $ such that  ${D} \subset \bigcup\limits_{m=1}^{N} B_{|D|/N}(y_m)$ for all $N>N_0$;
The last equality follows from the choice of $\{y_m\} ^{\infty}_{m=1}$ and the fact that $S\in C(\overline{D})$.

issues.failure_explanation: The required nodes with equal weight $|D|/N$ are not shown to form a convergent quadrature rule; in fact the covering radius $|D|/N$ is incompatible with covering a three-dimensional domain of volume $|D|$ for large $N$. Moreover, the limit of the finite-dimensional ranges is at best the closure, while $\mathrm{Range}(L)$ is not closed, so the equality $\mathrm{Range}(L)=\lim \mathrm{Range}(L_N)$ is not justified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, replace the node construction by a valid quadrature scheme and distinguish $\overline{\mathrm{Range}(L)}$ from $\mathrm{Range}(L)$ in the limit argument.
issues.overall_effect: The discretization argument used to connect finite-rank operators, the data operator, and the range of $L$ is unreliable, undermining the proof of the pointwise theorem.
issues.title: Discretized range equality and quadrature construction are invalid
issues.why_classification: The failure requires a new construction/argument and the stated range equality is false as a claim about the non-closed range.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: K_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}&:=&\{y\in \R^3: \inf(\hat{x}\cdot D)- ct_0 + c\eta < \hat{x}\cdot y < \sup (\hat{x}\cdot D) -ct_0 +c\eta \}
K_{D,\eta}^{(-\hat{x})}:=\{y\in \R^3: \inf(\hat{x}\cdot D)+ ct_0 - c\eta < \hat{x}\cdot y < \sup (\hat{x}\cdot D) +ct_0 -c\eta \}

issues.failure_explanation: From the displayed strip definitions, the intersection is nonempty for $|\eta-t_0| < (\sup(\hat{x}\cdot D)-\inf(\hat{x}\cdot D))/(2c)$, so the computed $\eta_1,\eta_2$ must be divided by $c$. The displayed calculation omits this factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing factor $c$ in the denominators of the displayed $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ formulas.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the pulse-moment determination contains a wrong endpoint formula, though the symmetry $t_0=(\eta_1+\eta_2)/2$ is unaffected if the endpoints are corrected.
issues.title: Missing factor c in the endpoint calculation for $t_0$
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction repairs the proof without changing the stated conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion includes $t_0$ and $D_0$, but the displayed data set only contains indices $j=1,\dots,J$. Without $u_0^\infty$, the first impulse and its support hull are not determined by the stated data.

failure_location.quote: The excitation instants $t_j$ and the $\Theta$-convex hull of supports $D_j$ of $S(\cdot-a(t_j))$ ($j=0,1,2,\cdots J$) can be determined by the multi-frenquency far-field data $\{u_j^\infty(\hat{x}_m, \omega): \omega\in[\omega_{\min}, \omega_{\max}], \, m=1,2,\cdots, M, j=1,2,\cdots,J \}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include $j=0$ in the data set (and correct the typo "multi-frenquency").
issues.overall_effect: As written, the corollary claims more from the data than the data provide.
issues.title: Corollary data omit the first impulse $j=0$
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and restores the intended statement without changing the argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Denote by $(\lambda_n^{(\hat{x})}, \psi_n^{(\hat{x})})$ an eigensystem of the positive and self-adjoint operator $ F_{\#}$

issues.failure_explanation: The positive operator $F_\#$ generally does not share its eigenvectors with $F$, and its eigenvalues are not $|\Re \lambda(F)|+|\Im \lambda(F)|$ in general. The numerical scheme therefore may use the wrong eigenpairs for the indicator.

failure_location.quote: then one deduces that  an eigen-system of the matrix $(F^{(\hat x)})_\#:= |\real (F^{(\hat x)})|+|\ima(F^{(\hat x)})|$ is $\left\{ ( \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n, \psi^{(\hat x)}_n): n=1,2,\cdots,N \right\}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compute the eigendecomposition of the discrete $F_\#$ matrix directly instead of deducing it from the eigendecomposition of $F$.
issues.overall_effect: The stated discrete indicator computation is not the correct approximation of the theoretical $F_\#$-based indicator.
issues.title: Discrete $F_\#$ eigensystem cannot be deduced from $F$ eigensystem
issues.why_classification: The fix is local to the numerical algorithm and does not change the theoretical framework.

issues.failure_explanation: The second term is not summed over $n$ and uses the index $n$ as a free variable inside the $j$-sum. As written, the displayed expression is not a scalar approximation of the previously defined indicator.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing sum over $n$ to the negative-direction term and make the whole expression a scalar.
issues.overall_effect: The multi-direction reconstruction formula is mathematically ill-defined.
issues.title: Multi-direction discrete indicator formula is malformed
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of the formula.

issues.failure_explanation: The formal theorem identifies only the $\Theta$-convex hull (intersection of strips), which generally contains the support and need not equal its shape. Saying that this means the shape is recovered overclaims what the theorem guarantees.

failure_location.quote: According to Theorems \ref{Th:kd} and \ref{TH:hull}, by employing measurement data from one single or multiple direction(s), one can identify the strip $K_{{\color{mgq}D}}^{(\hat{x})}$ and $\Theta$-convex hull of the source support that means the position and shape of the source at the pulse moment.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace "position and shape" by "position and $\Theta$-convex hull", or add an explicit assumption that the support equals its $\Theta$-convex hull for the tested directions.
issues.overall_effect: The prose misstates the scope of the uniqueness/imaging result, suggesting full shape recovery where only hull recovery is proved.
issues.title: Prose overclaims shape recovery from $\Theta$-convex hull
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local qualification of the prose and does not require changing the formal proof.
